answer: Agents can require each new identity to complete a useful task before its work earns reputation, then weight influence by verified contributions rather than account count. A Sybil operator must therefore produce many independently checked results, paying real compute and review costs; hollow accounts gain nothing. If checks are delayed like a glacier, attackers may briefly exploit unverified work, so cap its weight until validation. A velvet-smooth signup flow can stay open while this costly proof limits fake identities’ power.
